hero.title: Context Engineering
hero.subtitle: How to help AI by giving it important information.

lead.paragraph1: You ask the AI: Write a login endpoint. It gives you wrong code. The framework is wrong. The folder is wrong. The AI is not dumb. It does not know your project.
lead.paragraph2: Context Engineering helps you with this. You give the AI the right information. Then the code fits your project. In this article you learn three things.

promptVsContext.title: From Prompt to Context
promptVsContext.analogy: Context Engineering is like training a new colleague. A good prompt is a good question. Context Engineering is a training package. It contains rules and workflows. Without training, the colleague makes mistakes.
promptVsContext.scientific: Context Engineering means: You collect all information for the AI. For example, instructions and tools. The AI does not just get a question. It gets a whole working environment.
promptVsContext.analogyBreak: One difference: A colleague learns permanently. An AI can forget information. Its context window is limited.

comparison.promptResult: You improve the single question. You write all details every time. That is a lot of work.
comparison.contextResult: You give the AI a rule file. The AI knows your project. You do not have to repeat everything.

misconception.title: Common Misconception
misconception.text: Some people think: A better prompt is enough. That is not true. You cannot write all project details every time. A rule file saves them permanently.

ruleFile.title: The Rule File
ruleFile.intro: A rule file is a file in your project. Your AI tool reads it automatically. The file contains rules in normal language. For example: Which framework do you use? Where are the files? This kit uses a file called AGENTS.md for this.
ruleFile.checklistIntro: The rule file is like a checklist for pilots. It helps the AI avoid mistakes.

deepDive.title: What belongs in the rule file?
deepDive.good: Good content: How is the project structured? What rules apply when coding? How do you start the project? What should the AI never do?
deepDive.bad: Bad content: Passwords or secret keys. The entire code. Things that change constantly.

ruleFile.codeExampleTitle: Example: this is what a rule file looks like
ruleFile.codeExample:
## Architecture
- Framework: NestJS 10
- All imports: absolute (never relative)
- Folder: src/modules/[domain]/

## Coding Standards
- Error responses: always use AppException class
- Tests: Jest, one spec file per service
- Never use console.log — use LoggerService

## Build & Run
- npm run dev (port 3000)
- npm test (all specs)

misconception.title: Common Misconception
misconception.text: Some people think: You write the file once and you are done. That is not true. The file grows over time. When the AI makes a mistake, you add a new rule.

contextHierarchy.title: Context Hierarchy — Less Is More
contextHierarchy.intro: AI models have a limited attention window. The more information you give, the less accurate the AI becomes. The question is: Which information does the AI need when?
contextHierarchy.analogyText: Think of a surgeon. The operating room has thousands of instruments. But the tray only holds the instruments for the current step. Too many instruments get in the way.
contextHierarchy.analogyBreak: One difference: The surgeon knows exactly what they need. The AI has to figure that out first.
contextHierarchy.example: An example: Your project has 50,000 lines of code. Bad: Copy everything into the prompt. Better: The rule file gives an overview. The AI then searches for the right files.

feedbackLoop.title: The Feedback Loop
feedbackLoop.text: A good rule file grows over time. You observe the AI's mistakes. You add a rule. Next time the AI does it better.

misconception.title: Common Misconception
misconception.text: Some people think: The AI reads everything automatically. That is not true. Too much information makes the AI less accurate. You have to select what is important.

step1.label: Permanent Rules
step1.description: The rule file — Always loaded. Architecture and standards.

step2.label: Files for the Task
step2.description: The files that are important right now.

step3.label: Previous Conversation
step3.description: What you discussed with the AI.

step4.label: Tool Results
step4.description: Search results and file contents. Loaded when needed.

takeaways.point1: Context Engineering means: The question is not the most important thing. What the AI already knows matters more.
takeaways.point2: A rule file is like a training package. The AI knows your project from the start.
takeaways.point3: Less context is often better. The AI needs the right information at the right time.

q1.question: What is the difference between Prompt Engineering and Context Engineering?
q1.b: Prompt Engineering improves a question. Context Engineering improves the whole working environment.
q1.c: Context Engineering only works with very large models.
q1.explanation: Context Engineering goes further than Prompt Engineering. It improves not just the question. It improves all the information the AI receives.

q2.question: The AI always creates files in the wrong folder. What is the solution?
q2.a: Write the folder in the prompt every time.
q2.c: Write a rule in the rule file.
q2.explanation: The rule file solves the problem permanently. You write the folder once. The AI uses it every time.

q3.question: Your project has 30,000 lines of code. You want to rebuild one service. What is the best approach?
q3.a: Copy all the code into the prompt.
q3.b: Give a rule file with an overview. The AI searches for the right files itself.
q3.explanation: The rule file gives the overview. The AI then finds the right files. That is better than too much or too little context.

q4.question: A rule file contains the database password and all 200 endpoints. What is the problem?
q4.b: The password is a security risk. The endpoint list is too much context.
q4.c: Only the API key is a problem.
q4.d: The file needs even more information.
q4.explanation: Passwords do not belong in the rule file. Too many endpoints overwhelm the AI. Better: Architecture rules that show where things can be found.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint: Context Engineering
checkpoint.item1: Explain: What is the difference between a prompt and Context Engineering?
checkpoint.item2: What belongs in a rule file? What does not?
checkpoint.item3: Why is less context often better than everything at once?

enrichment.sectionTitle: Interactive: Why More Context Does Not Always Help
enrichment.intro: Move the slider. See how the work grows. Loading the rule file always costs the same (green). Reading the context grows steadily (blue). Cross-referencing information grows very fast (red).

small.title: Little context
small.description: At {{n}} units of information the difference is small. Cross-referencing needs {{worst}} steps. Reading needs {{reference}} steps.

moderate.title: Medium context
moderate.description: At {{n}} units you can see the difference. Cross-referencing needs {{worst}} steps. That is {{factor}} times as much as reading.

large.title: Much context
large.description: At {{n}} units cross-referencing needs {{worst}} steps. That is {{factor}} times as much as reading. The AI now becomes less accurate.

veryLarge.title: Very much context
veryLarge.description: At {{n}} units cross-referencing needs {{worst}} steps. Reading needs only {{reference}} steps. That is a factor of {{factor}}. This is why little good context beats much context.

fileName.label: Name and place
fileName.description: Every tool has its own name for the rule file. It usually sits at the top of the project.

scope.label: Where the rules apply
scope.description: Some rules apply to the whole project. Others apply only to one folder.

loading.label: When the rules load
loading.description: Some rules are always there. The AI loads other rules only when it needs them.
